Arithmetic from the brief: 7 Sep 2026 to 14 May 2027 = 35.7 weeks, minus 4 holiday weeks = ~31.7 study weeks; 130 GLH / 31.7 = ~4.1 tutored hours/week for maths. 7 Sep 2026 to 9 Jun 2027 = 39.4 weeks, minus 4 = ~35.4; 130 / 35.4 = ~3.7 hours/week for Spanish. claims.claim: Across 96 randomised trials of PreK-12 tutoring, tutoring raised achievement by about 0.37 SD on average; effects were larger for teacher and paraprofessional tutors than for parent or volunteer tutors, larger during the school day than after school, and maths effects persisted into later grades (source recalled, not confirmed by search this session).

claims.key_numbers: not shown in search summary (no search ran). Recalled and unverified: 96 RCTs, pooled effect about 0.37 SD; most programmes ran three or more sessions a week.
claims.implication: Tutor structure and quality drive the effect and no AI tutor was in the sample, so the 0.37 SD figure cannot be assumed to transfer to Claude-as-tutor. The Dec 2026 Foundation mock is therefore the first real test of whether this system works at grade-5 level; the parent should have a human tutor or centre-run mock as a pre-agreed fallback if it misses.

caveats: CRITICAL: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200 of 200) when this agent started; 10 targeted searches were issued (DfE early entry 2011-2013; Ofqual GLH; Dignath & Buttner 2008; Theobald 2021; EEF one-to-one tuition; Nickow, Oreopoulos & Quan 2020; home-educated GCSE outcomes; early-entry analyses 2024-2025; private-candidate NEA guidance; SRL interventions in adolescents with ADHD) and every one was refused, so searches_run is 0. No URL was obtained and no number was confirmed. Every source_title, authors_year and figure marked 'recalled' comes from model knowledge and must be verified before it is quoted to the parent; the verification agents should expect 'partial' at best on C1-C3, C5-C10 and C12.
C4 and C11 are the only claims grounded in material actually read this session (the system brief and a local skill file); C11's url is a local file path, not a web URL.
Theobald 2021 sampled university students; Dignath & Buttner 2008 is the only SRL meta-analysis here covering secondary-age pupils. Neither sampled people with ADHD.

The DfE 2011-2013 early-entry findings concern school-driven mass early entry (banking a grade C and not re-sitting); they are not evidence that an individual, readiness-based entry by a well-prepared younger student harms attainment. No study of readiness-based individual early entry was found or recalled.

The EEF and Nickow et al. tutoring evidence is about human tutors; no AI-tutoring evidence is included in this area and the 0.37 SD / +5 months figures should not be presented as expected gains from Claude-as-tutor.
No systematic data on home-educated students' GCSE outcomes in England exists to this agent's knowledge; small self-selected studies exist but none was retrievable, so none is cited.
The November-series age-16 rule (C12) is recalled from Ofqual's GCSE conditions and is load-bearing; confirm it against Ofqual or AQA before it is used in the tier/entry recommendation.
The GLH arithmetic in C3-C4 assumes 4 holiday weeks and a 7 Sep 2026 start; the brief records no weekly study hours, so the hours-per-week comparison cannot yet be checked against reality.
